en.name: Malabar spinach
en.summary: Malabar spinach is a climbing vine with thick, succulent, slightly mucilaginous leaves — not a true spinach at all, and considerably sturdier than one. No figure is published for it, so treat it like spinach: about 3–5 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Malabar spinach should not be kept at room temperature. The leaves are thick and hold up better than most greens, but they bruise easily and a bruise on a mucilaginous leaf turns black and slimy within hours in a warm kitchen. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Bag it unwashed and refrigerate it as soon as you get home.
en.fridge: Bag the leaves loosely without washing them and keep them in the crisper at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 3–5 days is the working limit — borrowed from spinach, since no figure is published for 皇宮菜 itself. The thick succulent leaves genuinely hold up better than most greens, but they bruise black where they are crushed, so do not pack the bag tight or stack anything on top of it. Wash only just before cooking; the leaf gel makes wet leaves go slimy quickly.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for Malabar spinach and freezing it is not worth doing. The leaves are succulent and full of water and a soluble gel, and freezing bursts the cells so that what thaws is a dark, slippery mass. Nothing unsafe happens; there is simply nothing worth putting on a plate. If you have too much, cook it now — it wilts down enormously, and is good stir-fried with garlic or dropped into a soup.
spoilage: Black or dark bruises spreading across the thick leaves
A slimy film on the leaves that does not rinse away
Stems gone soft and bendy instead of snapping
A sour or fermented smell in the bag
tips: Choose bunches with thick, firm, glossy leaves and no black bruising.
Bag them loosely and put nothing on top; bruises are what end this vegetable.
Separate the thicker stems and start them in the pan a minute before the leaves.
Stir-fry hot and fast with garlic; long cooking makes the mucilage pronounced.

faq.q: How long does Malabar spinach last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, bagged loosely and unwashed. That figure is borrowed from spinach; none is published for Malabar spinach.
No timeline exists and it is not worth doing. The succulent leaves collapse into a slippery mass on thawing.

faq.q: Is Malabar spinach the same as spinach?
faq.a: No. It is a tropical climbing vine from a different family, with much thicker leaves and a slightly slippery texture. It also stands up to heat and humidity where true spinach does not.
It contains mucilage, a soluble gel like okra's. Cooking it fast over high heat keeps that in check; long simmering brings it out.

zh.name: 皇宮菜
zh.summary: 皇宮菜是蔓性的攀緣植物，葉片厚實多汁、略帶黏滑，其實和真正的菠菜毫無關係，而且耐放得多。它沒有公布的保存數據，可以比照菠菜來看：4°C 以下冷藏約 3～5 天。
zh.pantry: 皇宮菜不應該放室溫。葉片厚，表現比多數葉菜好，但它很容易碰傷，而在溫暖的廚房裡，帶黏質的葉子一旦碰傷，幾小時內就會發黑變黏。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。買回家請不清洗裝袋直接冷藏。
zh.fridge: 不清洗，鬆鬆裝袋放在 4°C 以下的蔬果保鮮室，約 3～5 天是工作上限——這是比照菠菜而來，因為皇宮菜本身沒有公布的數據。厚實多汁的葉片確實比多數葉菜耐放，但被壓到的地方會瘀黑，所以袋子不要塞緊，上面也不要壓東西。要煮之前才洗；葉子的膠質會讓沾濕的葉片很快變黏。
zh.freezer: 皇宮菜沒有冷凍保存期限，冷凍也不值得。葉片肥厚多汁，充滿水分和可溶性膠質，冷凍會撐破細胞，解凍後只剩一團深色滑膩的東西。這不會有安全問題，只是沒有什麼能端上桌的了。真的太多的話，現在就煮吧——它一炒就縮得很少，蒜炒或丟進湯裡都很好。
spoilage: 厚葉上出現發黑的瘀傷並且擴散
葉面出現沖不掉的黏滑薄膜
tips: 挑葉片厚實挺硬、有光澤、沒有黑色瘀傷的。
鬆鬆裝袋，上面不要壓東西；碰傷才是終結這種菜的原因。
把比較粗的莖分開，比葉子早一分鐘下鍋。
大火快炒配蒜；久煮會讓黏液感變得很明顯。

faq.q: 皇宮菜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、不清洗鬆鬆裝袋，約 3～5 天。這個數字是比照菠菜而來；皇宮菜本身沒有公布的數據。
沒有對應的期限，也不值得。肥厚多汁的葉片解凍後會塌成滑膩的一團。
不一樣。它是不同科的熱帶蔓性植物，葉片厚得多、口感略帶滑潤，而且耐熱耐濕，真正的菠菜辦不到。
它含有黏質，就像秋葵那樣的可溶性膠質。大火快炒可以壓住那份滑感，久燉則會把它帶出來。
